purpose: a mini http server using only node built-ins in javascript
design: The design approach makes the code small and fast by using a lookup object (`routes`) for URL routing instead of an if/else chain, allowing for easy addition of new routes and a shared fallback response. This object-dispatch pattern is universal and can be applied to any state machine or lookup table, making it highly reusable and adaptable for other similar apps.

files.content: import http from 'http';import yargs from 'yargs';const { hostname, port } = yargs(process.argv.slice(2)).usage('$0 [options]').option('p', { alias: 'port', type: 'number', default: 3000 }).option('h', { alias: 'hostname', type: 'string', default: '127.0.0.1' }).help().parse();const routes = { '/': 'Hello World\n' };http.createServer((req, res) => {res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' });res.end(routes[req.url] ?? routes['/']);}).listen(port, hostname, () => console.log(`Server running at http://${hostname}:${port}/`));

lesson: The design approach makes the code small and fast by using a lookup object (`routes`) for URL routing instead of an if/else chain, allowing for easy addition of new routes and a shared fallback response. This object-dispatch pattern is universal and can be applied to any state machine or lookup table, making it highly reusable and adaptable for other similar apps.
